identification.summary: GoldFactory is the name Group-IB uses for a financially motivated, Chinese-speaking cybercrime group that develops and operates mobile banking malware (GoldDigger, GoldDiggerPlus, GoldKefu, GoldPickaxe for Android and iOS) against victims chiefly in Vietnam and Thailand [S1][S3]. Group-IB describes it as well organized and closely connected to the Gigabud malware family, and says it has been active since at least mid-2023 [S3][S5]. In December 2025 Group-IB reported a wave of modified legitimate banking apps hitting Indonesia, Thailand and Vietnam since October 2024, plus a pre-release test build it calls Gigaflower, a new Gigabud variant [S5][S6].
identification.firstObserved: 2023-06 (Group-IB: active since at least mid-2023; GoldDigger reported 2023-10) [S3][S5]
identification.notes: Single-vendor cluster (Group-IB); no Microsoft name or MITRE group ID identified in sources reviewed. Whether Gigabud and GoldFactory are directly the same operators is described in coverage as unresolved ('close connections') [S3]. Group-IB publications were seen only as search-result excerpts and secondary coverage; the primary pages could not be fetched.

attribution.confidence: Group-IB assesses GoldFactory as a Chinese-speaking cybercrime group [S3][S5]. No state sponsorship is asserted in the sources reviewed.
attribution.basis: Group-IB links the cluster by shared code and naming conventions across the 'Gold' malware families, and by close connections to Gigabud [S3]. The language assessment is Group-IB's, as relayed by secondary coverage [S3][S5].

objectives: Financial gain: theft of banking credentials, personal data, ID documents and facial recognition data, then account takeover and unauthorized transfers, including using AI face-swap deepfakes to defeat facial verification [S2][S3].

sectors: Banking and financial services customers (retail mobile banking users)
targeting.notes: GoldPickaxe lures impersonated Thai government services, including a Digital Pension app [S2]. Group-IB's December 2025 report counts 300+ modified banking-app samples and almost 2,200 infections in Indonesia; first cases of that wave were in Thailand, with Vietnam following and Indonesia surging from mid-2025 [S5][S6]. Lures impersonate government entities and trusted local brands, in one case Vietnam's EVN utility via Zalo [S5][S6]. Victims, not government or military networks, are the target set.

capabilities.summary: Social-engineering-led mobile malware operations. Android: GoldDigger abuses Accessibility Service to capture on-screen text including passwords; GoldDiggerPlus embeds GoldKefu, uses web fakes impersonating 10 Vietnamese banks and can place real-time calls to victims [S3]. GoldPickaxe (iOS and Android, derived from GoldDigger) collects facial data, ID documents and SMS [S1][S3]. iOS delivery first abused TestFlight, then tricked victims into installing an MDM profile giving broad device control [S2][S3]. Operators use AI face-swap services to produce deepfakes from stolen biometrics [S2][S3]. In the 2025 wave, legitimate banking apps are repackaged and modified to capture data and enable remote control [S5][S6]. Gigaflower is described as a pre-release test version of a new Gigabud variant with experimental features such as text recognition and QR scanning of ID card images [S5]. Lure delivery includes phone calls, messengers and fake Google Play pages leading to RATs such as Gigabud, MMRat or Remo [S5][S6].

campaigns.name: GoldDiggerPlus / GoldKefu first sample
campaigns.summary: Earliest GoldDiggerPlus sample carried an embedded second trojan, GoldKefu, using fake web pages impersonating 10 Vietnamese banks [S3].

campaigns.name: GoldDigger disclosed (Vietnam)
campaigns.summary: Group-IB reported GoldDigger, an Android trojan targeting Vietnamese financial institutions; GoldPickaxe distribution reportedly began around October 2023 [S2][S3].

campaigns.name: GoldPickaxe iOS and Android disclosed
campaigns.summary: Group-IB reported GoldPickaxe.iOS and an Android version stealing facial data, ID documents and SMS, with deepfake-enabled bypass of facial verification. iOS delivery moved from TestFlight to MDM profile, with Thai government (Digital Pension) lures. Thai police reportedly confirmed criminals used captured face scans to bypass facial recognition. HKCERT issued a public alert on 2024-02-20 [S1][S2][S3][S4].

campaigns.name: Modified banking-app wave begins (Thailand)
campaigns.summary: First cases of the later wave of repackaged banking apps appeared in Thailand in October 2024, followed by Vietnam in late 2024 to early 2025 [S5][S6].

campaigns.name: Indonesia surge
campaigns.summary: Infections rose sharply in Indonesia from mid-2025; Group-IB counted 300+ modified-app samples and almost 2,200 Indonesian infections [S5][S6].

campaigns.name: Group-IB 'Turning apps into gold' report and Gigaflower
campaigns.summary: Group-IB published findings on modified banking apps used against Indonesia, Thailand and Vietnam, and a pre-release Gigaflower build as a new Gigabud variant [S5][S6].

diamond.adversary: GoldFactory, Chinese-speaking cybercrime group per Group-IB, with close ties to the Gigabud ecosystem [S3][S5].
diamond.capability: Custom Android/iOS trojans, MDM abuse, AI face-swap deepfakes, repackaged banking apps [S2][S3][S6].
diamond.infrastructure: Fake Google Play pages, messenger links (LINE/Zalo-type channels), phone-call social engineering, fake government and brand apps [S2][S5][S6]. Specific C2 and domains not captured.
diamond.victim: Retail banking customers in Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia [S3][S5].
diamond.socioPolitical: Profit-driven fraud; no political aim stated in sources reviewed [S3].
diamond.technology: Android and iOS mobile platforms, TestFlight and MDM enrollment, accessibility services, facial-recognition banking checks, repackaged banking apps [S2][S3][S6].

gaps: Primary Group-IB reports (goldfactory-ios-trojan, turning-apps-into-gold) were visible only in search results and could not be opened; details rely on secondary coverage.
No Microsoft name, MITRE group ID, or government attribution found.
Relationship between GoldFactory and Gigabud operators is described only as 'close connections'; direct identity unconfirmed [S3].
No arrests or takedowns of operators found; Thai police statement is reported only secondhand [S3].
Infrastructure indicators, financial loss totals and operator identities not captured.
Exact publication day of the December 2025 report not verified.
Group-IB figures on 27 apps, 63% Indonesia share, 48 Gigaflower commands, hooking-tool names and the 50+ Vietnamese institutions count could not be confirmed and were removed.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. The actor is a criminal threat to personnel and families rather than to military networks. Step 1-2: operating environment includes Southeast Asian mobile banking users and personal devices; relevant terrain is app stores, MDM enrollment, messenger platforms and facial-verification banking [S2][S6]. Step 3-4 MLCOA: continued fraud against SE Asian retail banking users via impersonated government and brand lures, expanding country by country (Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia) [S5][S6]. MDCOA: expansion to other regions (Group-IB notes signs of geographic expansion) or to enterprise bring-your-own-device users, using stolen biometrics against corporate or financial verification [S3]. Candidate indicators: sideloaded banking apps, unexpected MDM profiles or TestFlight invitations, accessibility permission requests, unsolicited calls and messenger links from supposed utilities or agencies [S2][S5][S6].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: brief deployed and stationed personnel in Southeast Asia on mobile-banking fraud lures and biometric theft [S2][S5]. Authorities: this is criminal activity; response is through law enforcement and host-nation channels, with force protection and personnel-security advisories rather than offensive action. Mission assurance: restrict sideloading and unmanaged MDM enrollment on personal devices used for official duties and avoid sharing ID documents or face scans via apps [S2][S3]. Coordination: share indicators with security forces, counterintelligence and host-nation CERTs (Thai banking CERT and HKCERT already issued alerts) [S2][S4].

provenance.importedSummary: GoldFactory is a threat actor group attributed to developing sophisticated mobile banking malware targeting victims primarily in the Asia-Pacific region, specifically Vietnam and Thailand. They utilize social engineering to deliver malware to victims' devices and have close connections to the Gigabud malware family. GoldFactory's Trojans, such as GoldPickaxe and GoldDigger, employ tactics like smishing, phishing, and fake login screens to compromise victims' phones and steal sensitive information. Their evolving malware suite demonstrates a high level of operational maturity and ingenuity, requiring a proactive and multi-faceted cybersecurity approach to detect and mitigate their threats.
